# NGINX Upstream Block: Core Capabilities & Cheat Sheet
#### Generated by Google Gemini

The `upstream` block in NGINX is used to define a group of backend servers. It enables load balancing, failover, and advanced traffic routing, acting as the foundation for an API Gateway.

## 1. Load Balancing Algorithms

By default, NGINX distributes traffic sequentially (Round Robin). You can change this behavior by adding a directive at the top of the block.

* **`least_conn;`**: Sends new requests to the server with the fewest active connections. Ideal for applications where requests vary significantly in processing time (e.g., heavy database queries).
* **`ip_hash;`**: Uses the client's IP address to guarantee that the same user is always routed to the exact same backend server. Crucial for applications that rely on local in-memory sessions (e.g., shopping carts) rather than a shared database.

    upstream csharp_api {
        least_conn;
        server 172.28.1.10:5000;
        server 172.28.1.11:5000;
    }

## 2. Failover & Health Checks (Self-Healing)

NGINX actively tracks server health. If a server fails to respond, it is temporarily removed from the rotation so users do not see 502 errors.

* **`max_fails=[number]`**: The number of unsuccessful attempts to communicate with the server before NGINX considers it "down". Default is 1.
* **`fail_timeout=[time]`**: How long NGINX should wait before trying to send traffic to the "down" server again. Default is 10s.

    upstream backend_cluster {
        server 172.28.1.10:80 max_fails=3 fail_timeout=30s;
    }

## 3. Backup Servers (Disaster Recovery)

You can designate a server to sit entirely idle unless all primary servers in the upstream block crash.

* **`backup`**: Marks the server as a standby. It only receives traffic if the primary servers are unavailable. Perfect for displaying a static "Under Maintenance" HTML page.

    upstream primary_service {
        server 172.28.1.10:80;                # Primary
        server 172.28.1.99:80 backup;         # Standby Maintenance Page
    }

## 4. Traffic Weighting (Canary Deployments)

You can skew traffic distribution to favor specific servers, useful for testing new versions with a small subset of live users.

* **`weight=[number]`**: Sets the proportion of traffic the server receives relative to others. Default is 1.

    upstream rolling_deployment {
        server 172.28.1.10:5000 weight=9;   # V1 handles 90% of traffic
        server 172.28.1.20:5000 weight=1;   # V2 handles 10% of traffic
    }

## 5. Server State Management

You can manually mark a server as unavailable without removing its configuration line from the file.

* **`down`**: Marks the server as permanently offline. NGINX will not send any traffic to it until the `down` parameter is removed.

    upstream maintenance_mode {
        server 172.28.1.10:80 down;         # Temporarily offline for patching
        server 172.28.1.11:80;              # Handling all traffic
    }
